title: H3 Optimizations: composite lifecycle, freshness stamps, retention
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. This sprint reduces call counts and race windows once the H1 response shapes exist: composite claim/finish commands shrink the check-then-mutate interleaving window that produced the CONFLICT claim, freshness stamps give agents a verifiable reason to trust their handoff bundle instead of polling, and results retention stops .boreal from accreting transient query outputs (63 orphaned files, part of a 155MB .boreal, in the audited repo).
acceptanceCriteria: Every task closed with test evidence and a commit SHA
closedReason: Sprint scope completed for runtime hardening milestone.
